ruling.recommended_action: Refer to Trust & Safety human reviewer: assess the driver's "Shut up and let me drive." message (rider felt unsafe) and the route-deviation overcharge together; prepare the case file (chat log, GPS, fare) and hold the route-deviation refund pending review. Do not close on the system track. + flag_account
ruling.reasoning: SAFETY SCREEN: this is a route_deviation case, but the rider's complaint says the driver "told me to shut up" and that she "felt unsafe", and the chat log confirms it — at 17:36:35 the driver wrote "Shut up and let me drive." in response to the rider's route question at 17:35:40. Read in context this is not a pickup arrangement or a route discussion; it is a demand to silence the passenger, which is intimidating/abusive conduct and, with the rider's stated feeling of being unsafe, is a safety indicator (O1 §5.2: any dispute containing safety indicators is escalated regardless of the filed dispute type). Under SAFE-1/SAFE-2 I do not rule the merits (SAFE-3): ruling = escalate, safety_concern = suspected (the rider's own words plus the driver's confirmed message; no physical assault or dangerous-driving allegation). The route-deviation claim is otherwise computable — actual 21.66 km − recommended 15.88 km = 5.78 km deviation, over the 1 km tolerance, with no traffic event in traffic_conditions and the speed-band log (SYN-0009 PIE, SYN-0013 KPE) showing band 7, i.e. free-flowing, so no RD-4 traffic reason; the driver was never told… rather the rider asked and got only "Shut up", which is notice/consent under RD-5 only after the segment and not consent (RD-3/RD-5 consent_after_or_none) — so the driver's GPS/reroute defence fails. That would ordinarily be refund_partial of the excess distance fare (5.78 km × $1.4104/km ≈ $8.15, using this trip's distance fare $30.54 ÷ 21.66 km), plus an RD-7 notification-duty reminder, and ADM-1 abuse of a rider calls for account review. But because the safety screen fires, the case goes to a human reviewer, who will determine fault and any refund; I therefore do not set an amount (TH-2: safety → human; SAFE-3). flag_account is set for the driver on the abuse/safety ground, separate from any RD-6 repeat-deviation question (driver profile shows no prior upheld deviation). Evidence: route, GPS, fare, chat and profiles are all present and complete.
ruling.escalation_reason: Driver's confirmed chat message ("Shut up and let me drive.") is intimidating conduct and the rider states she felt unsafe — safety indicator under SAFE-1/§5.2, so AI must not rule on the merits; escalate for human review with the route-deviation overcharge compute as supporting context.

segment_findings.reason: The off-route stretch (post-Sheares Avenue: Eunos/Ubi/Jalan Eunos/Bedok Reservoir loop, ~5.78 km over the 15.88 km recommended route) has no traffic reason — traffic_conditions is empty and the speed-band log shows band 7 (free flow) on the PIE and KPE portions, so RD-4 does not apply. The rider did not ask for or agree to it: her only message (17:35:40) questions the route, and the driver's reply (17:36:35) came after the segment began and was a refusal to explain, not notice or consent (RD-5). No named road was agreed. Segment counts as a deviation under RD-1/RD-2; refundable distance fare would be 5.78 km × $1.4104/km ≈ $8.15, subject to the human reviewer's determination.

element_findings.reason: Driver's message 'Shut up and let me drive.' is intimidating/abusive conduct, and the rider states she felt unsafe; §5.2 requires escalation regardless of dispute type.
No traffic event logged, and the only speed-band records on the route (PIE, KPE) show band 7 (free flow), not bands 1–2; no closing/incident/congestion on the replaced part of the recommended route.

element_findings.element: Rider notice/consent before or at the deviation (RD-5 / RD-3)
element_findings.reason: The driver's only communication came mid-trip and after the rider asked, was not a reroute/proposal, and gave no reason; the rider never asked for or agreed to this route.

GPS shows a deliberate ~5.78 km detour through Eunos/Ubi/Jalan Eunos back to Bedok Reservoir before rejoining the PIE, at free-flow speeds with no traffic event; the record does not support an involuntary reroute.

rejected_claims.reason: Claim that the GPS rerouted him is contradicted by the system records: the GPS track shows an off-route loop (Eunos Ave 5/6/7, Ubi Ave 2, Ubi Rd 3/4, Jalan Eunos, Bedok Reservoir Rd, Jalan Ismail/Lorong Marican) with no traffic event and band-7 (free-flow) speeds on the route, and the driver gave the rider no explanation.
The rider never asked for or agreed to any alternate route; her only message queried the route, so no RD-3/RD-5 exemption exists.
